audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill/Skill/Skill/Neeko/Skill/Skill/Neeko, giving Neeko the two-item stage and denying her level 3 and level 6.
audit.why: The audited mirror settles it: Level 3 Neeko, Level 6 Neeko, two-plus items Trundle. The packet chart agrees, and whys[3] ('farm even and set up 6') and whys[6] ('full-item Trundle reclaims the duel') already said so in prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 3, 4 and 6 set to Neeko / Skill / Neeko / Trundle in both layers with matching ratings and whys.

audit.why: Mirror confirms the spike set: Blooming Burst 9s at 800, Shapesplitter 16s, Pop Blossom 120/105/90 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — level 3, level 6, first item, two items is the right shape.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ult setup was credited to 'invisible W' twice, and no string anywhere said what Tangle-Barbs actually does when it passes something.
audit.why: Riot's text: the tangle becomes larger, faster and roots for longer if it kills a unit or passes through a champion — so throwing it through a low minion upgrades the root. Neeko's W is a directional clone with a third-attack proc, no invisibility; the disguise is what hides Pop Blossom's preparation. Trundle's Pillar of Ice is terrain on 21/19.5/18/16.5/15s, and it displaces nothing.
audit.corrected: Tangle-Barbs' growth stated as the reason to shoot it through a minion, the disguise credited for the hidden preparation, and Pillar of Ice named with its cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Chomp is a flat 3.5s, Pillar of Ice is 21s at rank 1 and Subjugate 120/100/80 — those are the numbers that make 'wait, then go' concrete.
audit.corrected: Chomp's 3.5s and Pillar of Ice's 21s now appear in early and mid as explicit commit cues.

audit.whatIsWrong: No content-layer line told you to buy anti-heal, despite Frozen Domain amplifying all his healing.
audit.why: missingInteractions lists needs-antiheal (King's Tribute, Frozen Domain) and resistances-invalidated (King's Tribute, Subjugate) for this matchup.
audit.corrected: whys[5] now names Frozen Domain's healing amp and calls for anti-heal.

edits.before: Trade Q on his CS timings and hold E for the step-up. The disguise resets every bad position you take.
edits.after: Even: you cannot kill through King's Tribute sustain without ult, and Pillar of Ice walls off your approach.

edits.before: You're the teamfight flank now: disguise, walk into the clump, and R three people. Lane leads become fight wins.
edits.after: Subjugate steals your resists and heals him past one rotation — a full-item Trundle reclaims the duel outright.

edits.before: Q + E come online: root him with Tangle-Barbs and Q-bloom on top before his bite heals the trade back.
edits.after: Q + E online: send Tangle-Barbs through a minion so it arrives bigger and roots longer, then Q-bloom on top.

edits.before: Pop Blossom turns a landed E into a full stun-burst combo, unseen from a clone or invisible W — your best owning window before he tanks up.
edits.after: Pop Blossom turns a landed E into a full stun-burst combo, and the disguise hides the preparation — your best window before he tanks up.

edits.before: Your Liandry's/Blackfire spike helps in fights, but his pillar and bite keep the 1v1 a coin-flip — group instead of dueling.
edits.after: Your Liandry's/Blackfire spike helps in fights, but Frozen Domain amplifies his healing — bring anti-heal or group instead.

edits.before: Pop Blossom: ult from a clone or invisible W, land E, and the full combo forces his Flash or a chunk before Trundle's tankiness arrives.
edits.after: Pop Blossom: stay disguised so the preparation is hidden, land E first, and the combo forces his Flash before his tankiness arrives.

edits.before: Trundle is a drain-tank who wants to bite (Q) you and sustain through everything, so the early game is about chip, not all-ins. Levels 1-2 you only have single-target Q value — last-hit at max Q range and pre-bloom him when he steps to CS, but don't facecheck a trade he just heals back. At 3 you get Tangle-Barbs (E): root him in the line and immediately Q-bloom on top — that's your first real window before his sustain snowballs, but respect that he can drop his pillar (E) to wall off your approach.
edits.after: Trundle is a drain-tank who wants to Chomp you every 3.5 seconds and sustain through everything, so the early game is chip, not all-ins. Levels 1-2 you have single-target Q value only — last-hit from 800 and pre-bloom him when he steps to CS, but don't take a trade he simply heals back. At 3 you get Tangle-Barbs (E): throw it through a minion so it arrives larger and roots longer, then Q-bloom on top — your first real window, and respect that Pillar of Ice can wall off the follow-up.

edits.before: Through 4-5 you farm with Q-bloom and poke, but you won't all-in a sustain tank without ult, so trade and shove. Level 6 is your spike: set up Pop Blossom from a clone or W-invisibility so he can't see the channel, land E to lock him, and the stun-into-burst forces his Flash or a real chunk. Bait his pillar (E) — once it's down he has no peel against your combo. Don't over-extend chasing; he wants you to commit so his bite-sustain and pillar can flip it.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you farm with Q-bloom and poke, but you will not all-in a sustain tank without ult, so trade and shove. Level 6 is your spike: stay disguised so the Pop Blossom preparation stays hidden, land E to lock him, and the stun-into-burst forces his Flash or a real chunk. Bait Pillar of Ice first — it is 21s at rank 1, and without it he has no peel against your combo. Don't over-extend chasing; he wants the commit so Chomp sustain and the pillar flip it.

edits.before: Bite (Q) you to steal your AP-irrelevant AD and sustain through your Q poke
edits.after: Chomp you every 3.5s and heal off King's Tribute through your Q poke

edits.before: Drop E pillar to block your E line and your Pop Blossom approach, then walk you down
edits.after: Drop Pillar of Ice to block your E line and cut your retreat, then walk you down

notes: Packet 'games' is null here but the champion-level games count is 113 and the win rate 49.56%, so I treated it as live rather than deferring — flagging in case the intended rule was to skip on a null packet games field. Followed the mirror on the pillar: it creates terrain but displaces nothing, so I removed the claim that it blocks the Pop Blossom approach and left it as a retreat-cutter.
